tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start here. The README explains why this project exists â€” a config-driven authorization library with identical implementations in Spring Boot (Java) and NestJS (TypeScript), sharing language-neutral test vectors for cross-language parity. Read this first to understand the goals and project layout.
tour.languageLesson: Dual-implementation pattern â€” same behavior, two languages, shared test vectors as the source of truth.

tour.title: NestJS Library Entry
tour.description: createAuthz() is the single bootstrap function for the NestJS library. It orchestrates config loading, JWKS wiring, the startup state machine, and returns Express middleware plus runtime objects. The barrel index.ts re-exports everything for consumers.
tour.languageLesson: Bootstrap orchestrator pattern â€” a single function that wires the entire subsystem, returning a middleware + runtime object tuple.

tour.title: Spring Boot Entry
tour.description: AuthzAutoConfiguration is the Spring Boot auto-configuration entry point. It wires all beans â€” filter, engine, cache, sync, metrics â€” from the library JAR. Spring Boot's auto-configuration mechanism makes integration declarative with zero boilerplate.
tour.languageLesson: Auto-configuration pattern â€” @ConditionalOnXxx, @EnableConfigurationProperties, and spring.factories for zero-config library adoption.

tour.title: Rule Config Pipeline
tour.description: Both libraries compile authorization.yaml into compiled rules at startup. The YamlLoader/RuleCompiler parse path segments, assign wildcard scores, and validate fail-fast. Types.ts defines the rule schema. This is where configuration becomes executable policy.
tour.languageLesson: Fail-fast config â€” structural constraints (wildcard positions, segment kinds) checked at startup, not on first request.

tour.title: Decision Engine
tour.description: The core authorization engine matches requests against compiled rules using wildcard scoring (literal=2, *=1, **=0), then evaluates permissions against the role cache. The decision matrix handles USER, SERVICE, and USER_AND_SERVICE modes. Scoring resolves the most specific matching rule.
tour.languageLesson: Pattern matching with specificity scoring â€” a pure function that resolves ambiguity deterministically at request time.

tour.title: Permission Cache
tour.description: The in-memory permission cache stores role-to-permissions mappings with copy-on-replace semantics and versioning. This is the authoritative data source for all authorization decisions â€” no remote calls on the request path. The Spring Boot cache includes disk snapshot serialization for seed mode.
tour.languageLesson: Immutable cache with copy-on-replace â€” atomic swaps ensure readers never see partial updates on the hot path.

tour.title: Authentication & Context
tour.description: User JWTs and service tokens are validated against remote JWKS endpoints, then distilled into a RequestContext. The context builder strips untrusted identity headers to prevent spoofing. This context is the single source of truth for the requesting identity throughout the request lifecycle.
tour.languageLesson: Defense in depth â€” validate tokens at the boundary, strip incoming identity headers, build context from validated claims only.

tour.title: Service Tokens & SPI
tour.description: The service token provider acquires OAuth2 client-credentials tokens with caching and reactive refresh. SPI interfaces (TokenValidator, ServiceIdentityProvider, RoleResolver, etc.) define extension points for swapping implementations without changing auth logic.
tour.languageLesson: SPI pattern â€” interface-driven extensibility lets consumers replace caching, token validation, or role resolution without touching the core engine.

tour.title: Cache Sync & Bootstrap
tour.description: The startup state machine fetches the full role map from the Role Service, atomically replaces the cache, writes to disk, and subscribes to Kafka. If the Role Service is unreachable, disk cache seeds the in-memory store (seed mode). A periodic reconciler heals drift.
tour.languageLesson: Startup state machine â€” explicit SEED vs NORMAL mode with fail-open on Role Service unavailability, healed by periodic reconciler.

tour.title: Kafka & Role Events
tour.description: Incremental role updates arrive via Kafka topics (role-updates, role-delete, publish-roles). Events are applied to the cache in real time. A forced refresh on publish-roles re-fetches the full snapshot. Event processing includes validation and metrics counters.
tour.languageLesson: Event-driven cache invalidation â€” Kafka as the incremental transport, full snapshot as the healing mechanism, fail-open when Kafka is unreachable.

tour.title: NestJS Demo Service
tour.description: The NestJS demo is an Express host that calls createAuthz() to wire up the library, then registers business routes. The mock service provides JWKS endpoints, login, role service, and Kafka publishing for local development without real dependencies.
tour.languageLesson: Consumer-side integration â€” a single function call wires the entire auth middleware stack.

tour.title: Spring Boot Demo Service
tour.description: The Spring Boot demo uses @SpringBootApplication with auto-configuration â€” the library's AuthzAutoConfiguration wires everything. The authorization.yaml config defines route rules. Business controllers extract RequestContext for propagation verification but have no auth annotations.
tour.languageLesson: Global enforcement â€” no per-route opt-in; the AuthorizationFilter applies to all requests transparently.

tour.title: Global Enforcement
tour.description: Both libraries enforce authorization globally. The NestJS AuthzGuard is a CanActivate guard that validates tokens, builds context, evaluates the engine, and emits audit events. The Spring AuthorizationFilter is a OncePerRequestFilter with the same lifecycle. No per-route annotations needed.
tour.languageLesson: Framework filter/guard pattern â€” global enforcement with pluggable interceptors for outbound propagation.

tour.title: Test Vectors & Parity
tour.description: Language-neutral .vectors.json files define 29 scenarios covering decision modes, wildcard precedence, the full decision matrix, and edge cases. Both libraries load and assert against these same files â€” Jest for NestJS, JUnit 5 for Spring Boot. This is the cross-language correctness spine.
tour.languageLesson: Test vectors as executable specification â€” JSON files drive the same assertions in both language ecosystems.

tour.title: E2E & Infrastructure
tour.description: The end-to-end test stack runs both demo services, a Redpanda Kafka broker, and the mock service in Docker Compose. The run.mjs test driver sends the same HTTP scenarios to both services and asserts identical responses. Dockerfiles package each service for containerized deployment.
tour.languageLesson: Cross-language e2e â€” same requests, same assertions, two implementations. Docker Compose orchestrates the full dependency graph for CI.
